title: Carthage, Missouri at fourteen: shoeshine boy popping his rag
summary: Wanting extra money for clothes, he shined shoes at a hotel barbershop and added musical rag-popping that earned bigger tips.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yes, right, right. Well, before -- in fact, before I go into that, though, I would like to say that I made an error in saying where my music started. I forgot about one particular case that I told you about just now?
Before we came back to the tape, that I'd forgotten about. Before I had went into the army -- I must have been -- now at that time, I said 12, I said give or take, right?

So I must have been around 14 when this first surge into the music business hit me. We were in a town -- my father was preaching at a town, a church in a town Carthage, Missouri, C-a-r-t-h-a-g-e, Missouri. And we lived there and as I said my desire to pick up a little extra cash for myself, now was beginning to want more clothes, and I was called

embarrassed to ask my father for extra money because he might buy me a suit, you know, two pair of pants. But I'd want an extra pair of pants, or some shoes to go with it. So in order to buy the things that I wanted I needed to get some extra money.

So I went out and got a job as a shoe shine boy, and I wanted to show you a little something that used to make me a little money when I was shining shoes. If I can get the sound here (humming). See, I would take my rag and shine shoes like that. After having cleaned the horse manure off some of the shoes of some of the cowboys that'd come in, and they would only give you a dime, you know. But sometimes some of the more high class people would throw a little tip in there if I'd take the rag and pop it like that (humming). And they guy would say, that's a good shine, (can) you do that again. (Humming). Yeah, man, give me 15 cents.
So I'd get 15 cents for the shine, you know, maybe a quarter, you know.

And in fact, I had such a personality really, and I'll tell you as I live here, alive today, I did not really do this out of ego, I didn't do this out of anything to show off, it's just something that happened natural-ly. I wanted some money, you know, and the people -- some of these people, you know, like they just would -- this would be
a reason for them to give me extra money, to have me do this, and it was like show business.
